raw_response:
*sighs, sits down with tea*

Alright, let me think about this year. My husband and I have 14 mu — same as always. We're not young anymore, my back hurts in the mornings, so I have to be careful about how much work I take on.

**How I split the land:**
I'll put about 4 mu in cotton this year, same corner I always do — the soil there is a bit salty and cotton handles it better than wheat. The other 10 mu is wheat now, and after wheat comes out in June, maize goes in right away. That's how we've always done it. My neighbor Old Wang does the same.

**Wheat (10 mu):**
Wheat went in last October, so it's already in the ground — I'm thinking about what to do now that spring is here. The wheat looks okay, not too yellow. Before planting I put down about 3 bags of compound fertilizer per mu (the blue bag from the agro-shop, 15-15-15, 50 kg each). When it warms up and the wheat starts jointing, I'll topdress with urea — about half a bag per mu, maybe a bit more if it looks pale. That's what we always do.

I'll need to irrigate. Last year I watered three times — once before winter, once at jointing, once at heading. The well electricity is not cheap, 30-something yuan per mu each time, but if you don't water, the yield drops bad. Three times should be enough unless it's a very dry spring.

I'll spray herbicide once in spring — the weedy grass gets bad if you don't. My son-in-law sometimes helps with the sprayer on weekends. No insecticide unless I see aphids.

Harvest in early June — I hire the combine like everyone else, 60 yuan per mu. Save some seed for next year from the cleanest field, buy a little new seed to mix in.

Expect about 400 kg per mu. Last year was 420, year before was 380. It depends on the weather.

**Maize (10 mu, after wheat):**
As soon as the wheat combine finishes, we plant maize the next day or two — no time to waste, the heat is coming. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the shop has that year, about 40 yuan per mu worth. My husband drives the little planter we share with two other households.

Fertilizer: I drop about 2 bags of compound at planting, then topdress urea when the maize is knee-high, about half a bag per mu. If it rains enough I don't irrigate, but usually I water once in July when it's hot and dry.

Spray once for armyworm or corn borer if I see them. Otherwise leave it alone.

Harvest end of September, before the cotton picking gets really busy. Hire the combine again. Yield maybe 450 kg per mu in a good year.

**Cotton (4 mu):**
Cotton is the hard one. Plant mid-April, I still do it mostly by hand with my husband because the planter doesn't work well for cotton and hiring someone is expensive. I buy seed from the co-op, about 30 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, cotton needs less N than wheat — I put maybe 1.5 bags of compound at planting and topdress once when it starts flowering. Too much nitrogen and the plant grows tall but no bolls, my father-in-law taught me that.

Irrigate once or twice depending on rain. Spray for bollworm a couple times in July-August — this is the part that costs money and effort.

Then picking, starting September through October, multiple picks by hand. This is why I only keep 4 mu — my back can't do more. My daughter comes back from town for a weekend or two to help. Expect maybe 250 kg lint per mu, which is okay.

**Money:**
I don't want to spend too much. We have maybe 6-7 thousand yuan in the account for farm inputs. I buy fertilizer and seed at the village shop on credit sometimes and pay after harvest. That's how we manage.
